---
title: Recipes
description: Ready-to-use prompts for AI agents connected to WriteStack, with the tools each one calls, in order.
---

Each recipe is a prompt a writer can paste into Claude, ChatGPT or Notion once WriteStack is [connected](/docs/build), plus the tool calls a well-behaved agent makes. Use them to test an agent, or as building blocks in your own.

## Draft and queue Notes from a post

> Read my latest post and draft five Notes from it in my voice. Show them to me before saving.

1. `get_writing_style`
2. The post text or link the writer gives (or `get_article` if it is already a WriteStack article)
3. Show drafts, then `create_many_notes` with `status: "ready"`
4. `get_schedule_capacity`
5. Confirm the manual Sync step, then `schedule_notes` with `userConfirmedManualSync: true`
6. Remind the writer to click **Sync N scheduled notes to Substack** under **My Notes → Scheduled notes** ([why](/docs/using/concepts/sync))

## Fill next week's queue

> Fill my open slots for next week with my best ready Notes.

1. `get_schedule_capacity`
2. `get_next_available_slots`
3. `list_notes` with `status: "ready"`
4. `schedule_notes` (at most `remaining` Notes)

## Which Notes brought subscribers

> Which of my Notes from the last 30 days brought the most paid subscribers, and what do they have in common?

1. `get_notes_statistics` with a 30-day date range, sorted by subscribers
2. `get_note` on the top results for full text

## Turn a winner into new drafts

> Take my best Note this month and write three new angles on it.

1. `get_notes_statistics`
2. `get_writing_style`
3. `create_many_notes` with `status: "draft"`

## Reply to comments

> Show me comments and mentions from today that I haven't answered.

1. `list_activities` (paginate with `skip`, max `limit` 50)

The agent can draft replies, but posting replies happens in WriteStack or Substack.

## Write an article and push it to Substack

> Write a draft article from these notes for my main newsletter and push it to Substack as a draft.

1. `list_article_newsletters`, then ask which newsletter
2. `create_article` with that `publicationId`
3. `push_article_to_substack`
4. `get_article_substack_status` to show the draft link

Pushing runs through the writer's browser extension. With WriteStack open it usually finishes in seconds.

## Add an image that has no public link

> Add the chart from my Google Drive to the top of this article.

1. Get the file's bytes: download it from Drive, or read the local file
2. `create_article_image_upload` with the `articleId`, file name, exact `contentType` and exact `sizeBytes` (max 10 MB)
3. Within 15 minutes, send each entry in `parts` as a `PUT` of the raw bytes for that range, with the same `Content-Type`:
   - Up to 4 MB there is one part: `curl -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: image/png' --data-binary @chart.png '<uploadUrl>'`
   - A bigger file has 2 or 3 parts of 4 MB (the last one shorter). Send them in order and wait for each to succeed: `dd if=photo.jpg bs=4194304 skip=<part> count=1 2>/dev/null | curl -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: image/jpeg' --data-binary @- '<part url>'`
4. `get_article`, then `update_article` with `baseVersion`, and either `![alt](imageUrl)` in `bodyMarkdown` (to place it) or `imageUrl: [imageUrl]` (to add it at the end)

Every part uploads to `www.writestack.io`, so this works from sandboxes that can't reach Amazon S3. Uploading alone does not add the image. If the upload didn't finish, `update_article` says the image was skipped. An error response from a `PUT` says what didn't match (file type, part size or order, or an expired link). Fix it, or ask for new upload links.

## Cross-post a Note

> Schedule this Note and also post it to my LinkedIn through Buffer.

1. `list_buffer_channels`, then confirm the channel
2. `create_note` with `bufferChannelIds`
3. Schedule as above

## Ask the Coach

> Ask my WriteStack Coach what I should write about this week.

1. `ask_coach` with the question. Pass the returned `thread_id` to continue the same conversation.

This uses the writer's Coach allowance.
